recommendation: Keep this bounded source fix. No broader Consent model or terminology change is needed unless CBCC/Security later makes a new decision about hierarchical security-label interpretation.
issue_request: FHIR-36354 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent and asked the spec to clarify how Consent.provision.securityLabel codes from a hierarchical code system such as v3 Confidentiality should be interpreted for permit and deny provisions.
initial_application: PR #2132, commit da6cefb31d234cd244fc01b0fd93da66ec4d9726, and merge 991c8c5a5e9431e2f612ab039ce3ebc6c6e1c896 added the approved narrative to source/consent/consent-notes.xml. Current notes already state that subsumption must be considered and include the deny Restricted implies deny Very Restricted example.
additional_context: Consent is active in the current build via source/fhir.ini. The older StructureDefinition comment for Consent.provision.securityLabel still described only the R-or-lower high-water behavior, which matches the permit side but omitted the deny-side rule approved by FHIR-36354. FHIR-11056 is relevant background for older high-water wording, and later Consent restructuring in FHIR-39597 did not supersede the hierarchical code interpretation.
reconciliation: Updated source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml so the Consent.provision.securityLabel comment says hierarchical labels are interpreted in light of the matched provision decision: permit R includes R or lower, while deny R also denies higher-protection labels such as V.
source_changes: source/consent/structuredefinition-Consent.xml: clarified Consent.provision.securityLabel comment to distinguish permit and deny decisions for hierarchical Confidentiality labels.

related_jiras.note: Older Published Consent issue changed the securityLabel definition and documented confusion around high-water wording; it predates and does not supersede FHIR-36354.
Later Published Consent restructuring moved explicit provision type semantics to applicable decisions/inferred provision decisions, but did not reverse the FHIR-36354 hierarchical-code rule.
